Consider a function $f: R^{3 \cdot 2} → R^{3}$ defined by
$f(A) = A\begin{bmatrix}1 \\ 2\end{bmatrix}$.
Given that $a_{ij}$ denotes the entry of $A$ in the intersection of the $i$th row and $j$th column, we have$\frac{∂f_{3}}{∂a_{32}} =$ {{field-1}}.

Consider a function $f: R^{2 \cdot 2} → R^{2}$ defined by
$f(A) = \begin{bmatrix}1 & 5\end{bmatrix}A$.
Given that $a_{ij}$ denotes the entry of $A$ in the intersection of the $i$th row and $j$th column, we have$\frac{∂f_{1}}{∂a_{21}} =$ {{field-1}}.
